title: REAL WORK(N) — automatic array; allocated on entry, lifetime = subroutine call
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE PROCESS_BLOCK(IN, OUT, N)
C     The local array WORK is sized from the argument N. F90+
C     compilers allocate it from the stack on entry and free it on
C     return -- the lifetime IS the call. F77 forbade this (locals
C     had to have constant bounds), but real-world F77 code uses it
C     as a vendor extension.
C
C     A Java port using new float[N] inside the method works, but a
C     port that hoists WORK to a field (assuming SAVE-like
C     persistence) breaks re-entrancy.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER N, I
      REAL    IN(N), OUT(N)
      REAL    WORK(N)
      DO I = 1, N
         WORK(I) = IN(I) * 2.0
         OUT(I)  = WORK(I)
      END DO
      END
notes: Automatic arrays are the F90 generalisation of vendor F77 extensions (IBM XL Fortran, DEC Fortran). The lifetime contract matters: a hoist-to-class-field rewrite breaks any caller that depends on the per-call reset. Surface this whenever local arrays are sized from arguments.
